proof_summary: Quadratic reciprocity gives a square root of \(5\) modulo \(p\); choosing the even root \(2<r<p\) and setting \(n=r-1\) yields the continuant numerator \(r^2-5=pm\), where \(m\) is odd and sufficiently small. Scaled-continuant identities show that this small cofactor \(m\) divides the adjacent continuant, whereas \(p>n+1\) cannot divide it since any such common divisor would divide \(4(n-1)!\), so reduction cancels exactly \(m\) and leaves \(p\).
